title: Great app, wrongly rated
text:

Huge problem for me and my family, though: we use the Restrictions function for iPads and iPhones. We have removed browsers and limited web access to adult content and set the app install limit to apps rated 12+ or something like that. Google Photos is rated 4+ because Google told the App Store that they do not provide unrestricted web access. Well, they do. Unlike other apps, when you click the Privacy Policy link or something similar in this app’s settings, you get a page that can easily lead you to a google search page whose history is not kept. To get this search page, just keep clicking settings links on the webpages and trying to get to Google Account, from which you can find a link to google search. From there you can get to any website. And, it’s quite easy to come up with a search term that brings up porn in Images even with Apple’s setting turned on to Limit Adult Content.

I am writing this review as a shot in the dark, hoping Google will change it’s practice of putting those wide-open links in it’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy webpages and other such places. Every single Google app can get you unrestricted web access, even though Google reports to the App Store rating system that web access is not available. If they at least reported accurately, the apps would be rated 17+ instead of 4+.

title: The more I use it, the more problems arise.
text:
While I like the ability to back up my photos and search on Google Photos (by person, date, or content), the more I use the app, the more problems I see. I’ve used this app for years but almost no overwhelming upgrades have been made in that time. Unless you count being able to identify pets, which GP thinks my brothers dog and a llama are the same animal. 
1. It’ll identify people for you so that you can search for pictures of your cousin John or something of the sort. Except that the algorithm that Google uses to identify people is woefully inadequate. If the picture is unclear, they’re wearing a mask, it’s only their profile, it’s a picture from behind, or for no reason at all, Google doesn’t identify them as people, thus you can’t tag that photo for your own purposes. 
2. Not all photos get moved. I have a picture of a friend and I feeding a baby animal at a zoo. It’s STILL on my phone but not anywhere on GP. And there doesn’t seem to be any way to upload it to GP manually. So, if I’d deleted that on my device to make room, I’d have lost it forever. 
3. There’s been a continuous problem for  YEARS about scrolling. Sometimes in the search feature, it only lets you scroll so far and then pops you back up to a different point. It’s been a problem that has been complained about but no fix has been forthcoming. 
Right now, it seems to be the best app for this photo storage with it's features. However, it is far from ideal and Google is such an innovative company that you have to assume that these issues aren’t being addressed on purpose.
